_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Dubai v3 fleet-investors gold master per the international addendum (UAE/GCC run — tourism-weighted utilization stack). Sources: saudi-eastern-province/REVENUE-INPUTS-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md + FARE-BENCHMARKS-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md + CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md + DEMAND-POOLS-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md + SPEED-RULES-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md + NODES-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md. CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty content firewalls apply in full. Utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows are never summed into base totals; the tourism experience layer is the headline layer per the international addendum. All scenario figures computed from the REVENUE-INPUTS worked inputs and re-verified by script before writing ($0 diff). Demand pools are sourced census/project/traffic flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists. No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced Eastern Province fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders. Berthing and insurance are UNSOURCED in this market and are EXCLUDED from all totals, disclosed on-page (fn12) — unlike Dubai, which carried placeholders. Sponsorship and cargo upside rows render UNPRICED (local rates unsourced).

fn1.text: Experience and charter pricing is positioned against the water-leisure market operating on this coast today: houseboat hire published at SAR 690 per hour weekday and SAR 850 for the first weekend hour, short shared rides near SAR 100 per person, and small-yacht charters listed at SAR 1,000–2,500 per hour.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced census, project and traffic figures, not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are unpriced until local rates are sourced, and are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times use a conservative planning basis: slow transit near berths, beaches and shallow bays, service speed only on open coastal legs. Route, lane and speed terms are set with the sailing permit under the Kingdom's maritime security and safety regulations — favorable terms are upside, never in base times.

fn5.text: Seat pricing is a derived band, not a local quote: committed seats anchor to the corridor's ride-hail commute cost (about SAR 2,400 a month), point-to-point taxi at SAR 75–95, and the public intercity bus floor; spot fares sit inside the same substitutes. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a Saudi-adapted method: local job-market wage evidence for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), plus explicitly stated employment costs — social insurance, end-of-service accrual, housing and transport allowances. The model uses $33.5 per hour loaded, the mid benchmark; the low benchmark is $19.9.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded down to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: The conservative case assumes deliberately thin fills and pays back in about 33 years — shown as the floor, not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year. June–September heat shifts midday leisure sailings toward morning and evening slots; the Ramadan month shifts leisure to the hours after iftar and thins daytime commuting; November–March is the corniche high season. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with that shape absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at the published Saudi commercial electricity tariff for high-volume connections — about $0.085 per kWh. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line rises about 3.5×, and every scenario remains cash-positive.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Local benchmarks are cited in Saudi riyals and convert at the pegged rate of 3.75 riyals per dollar.

fn12.text: Berthing and insurance are excluded from the totals shown: no published berth rate card exists for the corniche marinas and no Saudi marine hull benchmark was sourced. Quotes are the open item, and both lines will reduce net when they land.

fn13.text: The Dammam–Khobar drive runs about 15 minutes off-peak — on an empty highway the road wins. The spine's case is the corridor's documented peak congestion, the cruise-terminal connection and the corniche-to-corniche experience; the resort-bay line is the time-competitive run when weekend traffic stacks up.

fn14.text: Roadmap items render as reach only: Uqair's heritage port has an announced development program and no passenger landing today, and a Khobar–Bahrain water link appears with no schedule and no economics.

_internal.sources: REVENUE-INPUTS-EASTERN-PROVINCE.md (bands, scenario inputs, opex inputs). Crew: CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS (SAUDI-ADAPTED, LOW $19.9 / MID $33.5; model uses MID in all tiers per instruction, LOW as sensitivity fn6). Energy: SEC/SERA commercial >6,000 kWh/mo = SAR 0.32/kWh = $0.0853/kWh (PRIMARY) × 4.1 kWh/nm = ~$0.35/nm.
_internal.commute_capacity_basis: 8 commute legs/day (4 AM + 4 PM sailings on the ~42-min EP-1 spine) × 20 seats × 22 weekdays = 3,520 commute seat-legs/mo. Committed riders take 44 legs/mo (22 days × 2); residual seat-legs = 3,520 − committed × 44.
_internal.committed_seats_basis: Per-vessel committed seats 15/30/50 = REVENUE-INPUTS network-wide penetration scenarios (LOW 60 / MID 120 / HIGH 200) spread across a four-vessel reference fleet — DERIVED assumption, no OD survey exists (fail-closed register); labeled indicative, never rendered as rider counts. Feasibility: upside 50 riders × 2 legs/day = 100 seat-legs/day vs 160 available.

opex_basis.crew: Per-scenario activity hours × $33.5/hr MID: hours = (132 commute + experience sailings × 1.5 + charter hrs) × 1.1 positioning overhead → 180/216/252 hrs = $6,030/$7,236/$8,442; rendered as the band.
opex_basis.energy: Monthly nm: commute 8 × 15.1 nm × 22 = 2,658 + experiences × ~14 nm (224/448/672) + charters × ~12 nm/hr (96/192/288) = 2,978/3,298/3,618 nm × $0.35/nm = $1,042/$1,154/$1,266. Sensitivity at $0.30/kWh ($1.23/nm): line rises ~3.5× (+$2.6–3.2K/mo); nets stay positive in all scenarios (fn10: conservative net falls to ~$3.6K/mo).
opex_basis.maintenance: $82.5K/yr = $6,875/mo, program-consistent N45 figure, flat across scenarios.
opex_basis.berthing_insurance: EXCLUDED from totals per instruction — berthing rate cards not public (Amanah/marina quotes required), no KSA marine hull benchmark. Disclosed on-page via the null-value opex row + fn12. Placeholder magnitude if quoted at Dubai-like levels would be several $K/mo — conservative payback would extend materially; flagged for Jaideep.

_internal.opex_total_note: Opex varies by scenario (crew + energy scale): $13,947 / $15,265 / $16,583 — rendered as the conservative-to-upside band. Scenario nets reflect per-scenario opex.

layer_pricing_basis.committed_bundles_L1: DERIVED $550/$650/$750 per seat-month (REVENUE-INPUTS recommended band, ~0.85–1.15× the SAR 2,420/mo all-ride-hail commute substitute). 15/30/50 seats per scenario. Status everywhere: modeled + fn5. Needs Jaideep confirmation before external quoting.
layer_pricing_basis.spot_seats_L2: $16/$20/$25 per leg (EP-1 band SAR 60–95) × 10/20/30% fill of residual seat-legs (2,860/2,200/1,320). Seats: 286/440/396 — all whole numbers this run; seat count × fare is the exact line (fn7). Upside spot revenue is LOWER than mid because the committed book absorbs residual capacity — rendered honestly.
layer_pricing_basis.experiences_charters_L3: Experiences $40/$50/$65 pp (inside derived SAR 150–250/pp band, anchored to HMB SAR 100–200/pp evidence) × 16/32/48 sailings × 10/12/14 seats. Charters $400/$525/$650 per hr (SAR 1,500–2,437 — inside the derived SAR 1,500–2,500 band, above houseboat SAR 690–850/hr PRIMARY, inside small-yacht SAR 1,000–2,500/hr SECONDARY) × 8/16/24 hrs.
layer_pricing_basis.sponsorship_U1: UNPRICED — REVENUE-INPUTS holds it unsized by design (no local sponsorship rate evidence). Renders as unpriced upside row only.
layer_pricing_basis.overnight_cargo_U2: UNPRICED — no local courier rate card sourced; held out of math per REVENUE-INPUTS. Renders as unpriced upside row only.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.
